placements.why: This envelope's whole content is an engineering-infrastructure decision (a database engine migration) argued on performance and licensing-cost grounds and scheduled to a quarter. No strata category exists yet in this repo, and nothing in the supplied (empty) strata covers organizational-architecture content — Architecture is the canonical top-level category this taxonomy names for exactly this kind of decision, and it needs no parent minted first.
placements.title: Engineering infrastructure and technical architecture decisions
placements.frame: What infrastructure, platform, or architecture choices is the org making, and what tradeoffs (performance, cost, risk) drive them?

placements.title: Analytics infrastructure shifts from general-purpose relational databases to specialized high-performance engines
placements.frame: What performance, cost, or licensing tradeoffs are driving migrations of core data infrastructure, and how are those decisions justified, ratified, and scheduled?
placements.why: src-1 and src-3 perform the PostgreSQL-to-QuantumDB switch as a settled, ratified decision (spoken and summarized); src-2 and src-4 supply the recurring justification pattern — quantified performance gain plus reduced licensing cost — that this kind of infrastructure decision is argued on; src-5 anchors the same move to a concrete quarter. None of these is, alone, a leaf-grade theme (the specific tool names and the Q3 2026 date are facts true only of this migration), but together they instantiate a pattern future infrastructure envelopes plausibly keep feeding: infrastructure choices driven by performance/cost calculus and executed on a schedule. That pattern, not the one-time swap itself, is what the leaf holds.
